mission: Give Buddy and the DreamCo coding fleet a structured path to master global software-engineering knowledge, compare public engineering techniques across ecosystems and regions, invent new abstractions when justified, and design original programming languages, DSLs, bytecode formats, compilers, runtimes, or binary-oriented representations with measurable advantages.
truth_boundary: No system can literally contain all coding knowledge. Buddy should continuously index, verify, retrieve, benchmark, and refresh the world's accessible lawful software-engineering knowledge instead of claiming omniscience.
global_learning_sources: open model and AI engineering reports

country_and_region_comparison.goal: Compare public engineering ecosystems and techniques by evidence, not stereotypes or nationality assumptions.

mastery_cycle: discover a topic, implementation, library, language, compiler, runtime, or technique
classify it in the Universal Training Library
record provenance, version, license, environment and source freshness
build an executable skill card and minimal reproduction
test normal, hard, edge and failure cases
benchmark against alternatives using identical fixtures
extract reusable principles rather than copying incompatible implementation details
promote reusable improvements to shared coding infrastructure
record gaps and assign parallel builder competition lanes
refresh or deprecate knowledge when upstream changes

language_invention_program.principle: Invent a new language only when it solves a measured problem better than existing languages, libraries, DSLs, transpilers, or configuration systems.
design_stages: decide whether a library/DSL/transpiler is enough before inventing a full language
choose native, LLVM-like IR, C/C++, WebAssembly, JVM, .NET, GPU, or custom VM targets as appropriate
build formatter, linter, debugger, package tooling and language-server support
benchmark readability, correctness, performance, binary size, compile time, runtime memory, energy-relevant work, safety and developer time
dogfood inside DreamCo before public release
version language/spec and maintain backward-compatible upgrade tooling

binary_and_zero_one_research.goal: Explore representations closer to machine execution without forcing humans to author raw bitstrings unnecessarily.
invention_options: human-friendly symbolic syntax that compiles to compact binary
AI-oriented intermediate representation optimized for generation and verification
binary schema language with automatic safe encoders/decoders
binary_and_zero_one_research.rule: Raw 0/1 authoring is a learning/debugging tool, not the default user interface unless a benchmark proves it is superior for a specific machine-to-machine use case.

questions: What task is still too slow, expensive, unsafe, repetitive or difficult?
Which proven techniques from different ecosystems can be composed lawfully?
Can a shared abstraction remove duplicated code across many bots?
Can a compiler/runtime transformation remove work from the user?
Can a local-first implementation improve privacy and cost?
Can stronger typing, verification or schemas eliminate a recurring class of bugs?
Can better representations reduce tokens, memory, bandwidth, storage or compute?
Can Buddy generate tooling around the technique so ordinary users can benefit?

united_states_technology_advancement.goal: Use lawful global technical learning to build original DreamCo engineering capability, education, tools, benchmarks, open standards, products, and training programs that strengthen U.S.-based coding and technology capacity while remaining globally interoperable.
outputs: commercial training/data/skill packages with verified rights

competition_and_benchmarks.gap_rule: Every measured gap feeds the existing parallel benchmark-gap builder competition and shared-fleet inheritance system.

guardrails: respect licenses, patents, terms and attribution requirements
do not characterize a country's engineers or methods using stereotypes; compare specific public technical evidence
do not copy restricted proprietary code or confidential techniques
do not claim global mastery without current evidence coverage
do not invent a language merely for novelty
do not ship a new compiler/runtime without conformance, security, fuzzing, regression, upgrade and rollback testing
do not replace mature libraries/languages when integration is safer and more efficient
keep experimental machine-code and binary execution isolated until verified
promote reusable winning techniques into shared fleet infrastructure
